Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on broad depression.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: broad depression (BD)
Population: 113,769 broad depression cases and 208,811 controls; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: At baseline, 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels were significantly lower in premenopausal women with major depression than in healthy controls.
Sentence: "At baseline, ionized calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels were significantly lower in women with MDD compared to controls."
Measured as: major depressive disorder (MDD)
Population: Premenopausal women aged 21 to 45 years with major depressive disorder (n=92) and healthy controls (n=44)
Intervention: No intervention; baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level measured
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 136
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a Mendelian randomization estimate of genetically predicted vitamin D on broad depression, while Study B is a case-control comparison of baseline serum 25(OH)D in major depression; they measure different exposures and designs, and the MR null versus the observational lower-level association is a design difference.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population"],"detail":"design: Mendelian randomization vs case-control; outcome: broad depression vs major depressive disorder in premenopausal women"}
